editorial_criteria: For written-review tasks, assess the complete article, including title, opening, headings, figures, captions and ending, under writing-guide.md. Each sentence contributes meaning in context; paragraphs develop points and sections form a connected explanation. Fluency or varying sentence shapes alone does not establish continuity.

Report findings and uncertainty without directing what the reader should do or believe. Attributed guidance can remain as reported evidence. Accessible styles need no required personal address, named actors, plot twist, analogy recurrence or formulaic endings.

Locate unexplained jumps, source inventories, redundant returns and figures that separate a finding from its qualification. Distinguish defects from reasonable alternative organizations and permit parallel outcomes without inventing causal links.

Evaluate preserved comparisons, outcomes, uncertainty, contrary findings and source coverage separately from readability. Record passage-specific reasons and the reader's reconstructed answer; never treat a machine pass, source support or a word count as an editorial verdict.
